section: India - climate: mechanism of the monsoon, theories, seasons and their characteristics
subsections: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches
Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD

accepted.s: The normal date of onset of the southwest monsoon over Kerala is:
accepted.x: The normal onset date of the southwest monsoon over Kerala is 1 June.
accepted.tq: Use the exact date rather than confusing onset over the islands, advance dates and countrywide coverage.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The southwest monsoon normally reaches the Andaman and Nicobar Islands approximately on:
accepted.x: The southwest monsoon reaches the Andaman and Nicobar Islands at about 25 May, before its normal onset over Kerala.
accepted.tq: Separate the earliest island onset from the normal mainland onset.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the duration of the southwest monsoon in India:
1. It lasts for less than 75 days in western Rajasthan.
2. It lasts for more than 120 days in the south-western peninsula.
3. Its duration is uniform throughout the country.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The duration is less than 75 days in western Rajasthan and more than 120 days in the south-western peninsula. It is not uniform throughout India.
accepted.tq: Compare regional extremes and reject the absolute statement about uniformity.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the revised normal dates of the India Meteorological Department, the southwest monsoon covers the whole country by:
accepted.x: The IMD's revised normal date for the southwest monsoon to cover the whole country is 8 July.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the revised date from approximate descriptions such as ‘by the end of June’ or ‘by the end of July’.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The India Meteorological Department fixes the onset of the southwest monsoon primarily by examining rainfall over:
accepted.x: The IMD uses rainfall recorded over five-day pentads while fixing the onset of the southwest monsoon.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise operational time unit instead of choosing a broader climatological period.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the approximate advance of the southwest monsoon?
o: Bhopal by 15 June and Delhi by 25 June
Bhopal by 25 May and Delhi by 1 June
Bhopal by 1 July and Delhi by 8 July
Bhopal by 25 June and Delhi by 15 July
accepted.x: The southwest monsoon normally reaches Bhopal around 15 June and Delhi around 25 June.
accepted.tq: Use the sequence and paired dates to distinguish advance dates from onset and withdrawal dates.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The southwest monsoon generally covers the country in approximately:
accepted.x: After its onset and advance, the southwest monsoon covers the country in about one month.
accepted.tq: Test the approximate duration of a process rather than a single station date.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The IMD declaration of monsoon onset involves which of the following conditions after 10 May?
1. At least 60 per cent of 14 specified stations receive 2.5 mm of rain for two days.
2. Westerlies reach approximately the 600 hPa level.
3. The conditions are assessed only after the end of June.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The onset criteria include rainfall of 2.5 mm for two days at 60 per cent of 14 stations and westerlies reaching about 600 hPa after 10 May. They are not assessed only after June.
accepted.tq: Find the false timing statement while retaining the precise threshold conditions.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During a ‘break’ in the southwest monsoon, which one of the following conditions generally occurs?
o: The Arabian Sea branch reverses into a winter monsoon over the west coast.
The tropical easterly jet disappears and the westerly jet moves south of the Himalayas.
The monsoon trough shifts permanently to the Indian Ocean and all rainfall stops.
The monsoon trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills, leaving the plains relatively dry.
accepted.x: During a monsoon break, the trough shifts towards the Himalayan foothills. The plains consequently experience dry conditions while the Himalayan region receives heavy rainfall.
accepted.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect relationship between trough position and regional rainfall.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from India normally:
o: Begins in the south in May and ends in August
Begins in the north-west in October and ends by the end of November
Begins in the east in September and ends by mid-October
Begins simultaneously throughout India in November
accepted.x: Withdrawal begins from north-western India in October and is generally complete by the end of November.
accepted.tq: Remember the direction and time span of withdrawal rather than the onset sequence.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bay of Bengal branch — moves north along the western coast after crossing the Western Ghats
Arabian Sea branch — Agumbe and Hulikal receive very heavy rainfall
Arabian Sea branch — first strikes the Meghalaya hills
Bay of Bengal branch — produces a rain-shadow region immediately east of the Western Ghats
accepted.x: Agumbe and Hulikal receive very heavy rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch. The other descriptions interchange the paths and effects of the two branches.
accepted.tq: Use branch-specific routes and locations to eliminate swapped descriptions.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon?
o: It first reaches Myanmar and turns west along the Himalayan foothills.
It first affects the Western Ghats and the Malabar Coast, then moves north along the west coast.
It crosses the Himalayas and descends over the Ganga plains.
It originates over the Bay of Bengal and moves directly towards Meghalaya.
accepted.x: The Arabian Sea branch first strikes the Western Ghats and Malabar Coast and subsequently advances northward along the west coast.
accepted.tq: Trace the branch from its first landfall to its subsequent movement.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rain-shadow region associated with the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon lies mainly:
o: To the west of the Malabar Coast
To the east of the Western Ghats
accepted.x: The Western Ghats force uplift on their windward side, leaving a rain-shadow region to their east.
accepted.tq: Use the windward-leeward comparison to identify the rain-shadow location.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The southwest monsoon season contributes approximately what proportion of India's annual rainfall?
accepted.x: The southwest monsoon season provides about 75 per cent of India's annual rainfall.
accepted.tq: Select the stated national share without confusing it with regional rainfall percentages.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The long-period average annual rainfall of India for 1971–2020 is given as:
accepted.x: The long-period average annual rainfall cited for India for 1971–2020 is 868.6 mm.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact rainfall figure from nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following phenomena are associated with the retreating southwest monsoon?
1. The Sun moves southward and the north-western low-pressure area weakens.
2. The westerly jet returns south of the Himalayas.
3. The tropical easterly jet disappears.
4. Clear skies and ‘October heat’ are experienced.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four conditions accompany the retreating monsoon. The weakening of the north-western low, jet-stream changes and clear, hot weather are characteristic of October–November.
accepted.tq: Test a complete cluster of associated seasonal characteristics.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The bimodal rainfall received by parts of southern India during the retreating monsoon is mainly associated with:
o: The permanent high over the South Indian Ocean
accepted.x: Bay of Bengal cyclones bring bimodal rainfall to the south during the October–November retreating monsoon season.
accepted.tq: Match the seasonal rainfall feature with its immediate weather system.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes monsoon winds?
o: Local winds confined to mountain valleys
Polar winds that move towards the equator in all seasons
Permanent winds blowing in one direction throughout the year
Seasonal winds that reverse direction between summer and winter
accepted.x: Monsoons are seasonal winds that reverse direction: they generally blow from sea to land in summer and from land to sea in winter.
accepted.tq: Use the defining seasonal reversal to distinguish monsoons from permanent and local winds.
accepted.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the classical thermal theory of the monsoon, the summer monsoon is produced primarily because:
o: The ITCZ remains fixed south of the equator throughout the year.
Land heats faster than the sea, creating a low-pressure area over land that draws moist winds from the sea.
The Himalayas generate a cold high-pressure area over northern India in summer.
The sea heats faster than the land, creating a permanent low over the ocean.
accepted.x: Sir Edmund Halley's thermal theory, proposed in 1686, attributes the monsoon to differential heating of land and sea. Summer heating creates a low over land that attracts moist maritime winds.
accepted.tq: Apply the pressure-gradient logic of differential heating rather than memorising only the theory’s name.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who propounded the classical thermal theory of the monsoon in 1686?
accepted.x: Sir Edmund Halley propounded the classical thermal theory of the monsoon in 1686.
accepted.tq: Link the named theory with its associated scholar and year.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The dynamic or ITCZ theory explains the southwest monsoon mainly through:
o: The cooling of the Tibetan Plateau during the summer months.
The northward shift of the ITCZ over the Ganga plain, drawing south-east trade winds across the equator as south-westerlies.
The southward shift of the ITCZ over the Indian Ocean during summer.
The permanent eastward movement of the subtropical westerly jet over peninsular India.
accepted.x: In summer, the ITCZ shifts northward over the Ganga plain as the monsoon trough. South-east trades cross the equator and are deflected to become south-westerly winds.
accepted.tq: Follow the movement of the pressure belt and the cross-equatorial wind path.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about jet streams and the Indian monsoon:
1. The subtropical westerly jet shifts north of the Himalayas during summer.
2. The tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea towards East Africa.
3. The return of the subtropical westerly jet south of the Himalayas is associated with monsoon withdrawal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The northward shift of the subtropical westerly jet is associated with onset, while its return south of the Himalayas accompanies withdrawal; the tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea to East Africa.
accepted.tq: Combine onset, withdrawal and jet-stream path statements before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The heating of the Tibetan Plateau contributes to the southwest monsoon by:
o: Creating an upper-air anticyclone and strengthening the tropical easterly jet
Blocking all cross-equatorial winds in the Arabian Sea
Creating a permanent surface high and weakening the tropical easterly jet
Producing the subtropical westerly jet south of the Himalayas in summer
accepted.x: The Tibetan Plateau, at about 5,000 m, acts as a heat island in summer. Its intense heating produces an upper-air anticyclone and strengthens the tropical easterly jet.
accepted.tq: Connect plateau heating with its upper-air circulation effects.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the influence of ENSO on the Indian monsoon?
o: El Niño generally weakens the monsoon, whereas La Niña generally strengthens it.
El Niño always strengthens the monsoon, whereas La Niña weakens it.
ENSO has no relationship with monsoon variability.
Both El Niño and La Niña invariably weaken the monsoon.
accepted.x: El Niño generally weakens the Indian monsoon, while La Niña generally aids or strengthens it.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-effect trap in paired climate phenomena.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly represents the combined influence of IOD and MJO on the Indian monsoon?
o: An unfavourable MJO phase invariably produces a strong southwest monsoon.
A positive IOD can offset the adverse effect of El Niño, while an unfavourable MJO phase can stall the monsoon.
IOD affects only winter temperatures and MJO affects only Himalayan snowfall.
A positive IOD always eliminates El Niño, while every MJO phase strengthens rainfall.
accepted.x: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can partly offset the weakening influence of El Niño. An unfavourable phase of the Madden–Julian Oscillation can stall the monsoon.
accepted.tq: Separate the moderating role of IOD from the phase-dependent influence of MJO.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The modern complex explanation of the Indian monsoon mechanism is dated in the material to:
accepted.x: The modern complex explanation of the monsoon mechanism is dated to 1957.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the modern explanatory framework from the date of the classical thermal theory.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What would be the most significant climatic consequence for northern India if the Himalayas did not exist?
o: The southwest monsoon would reverse permanently into a north-easterly wind.
The region would receive heavier monsoon rainfall because cold air would enter freely.
Northern India would tend to become a desert because the Himalayas would no longer block cold Central Asian air or trap the monsoon.
The Tibetan Plateau would become a permanent oceanic low-pressure centre.
accepted.x: The Himalayas block cold Central Asian air and help trap the monsoon over the subcontinent. Without them, northern India would tend to become a desert.
accepted.tq: Apply the barrier and trapping functions of a major relief feature to a hypothetical situation.
accepted.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]
